In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the factors that promote the use of traditional biomass in Sub Sahara Africa are: (a) the low level of income and the associated low purchasing power of households (b) the low level and poor distribution of energy infrastructure (c) the lack of awareness of the health risks of traditional biomass use and (d) the high population density in some areas.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
energy use is spatially patterned in Africa and the spatial patterns are determined by factors that promote a spatial pattern.
the use of biomass in Ghana is not only a function of population but also of the spatial distribution of population.

the factors accounting for energy use in Ghana are not only limited to the traditional factors of population, income, and technology but also to the non traditional factors such as geography, culture and climate.

the spatial pattern in energy consumption is driven by the spatial pattern in population density and that this pattern is not changing.
